assumptions: The first buyers are complex small or mid-sized groups and compliance outsourcers with several entities and material ICT inventories, not the smallest proportionality-eligible firms.
The initial deployment is customer-controlled or suitably EU-hosted, all extracted values are human-approved, and the product does not replace the regulated entity's accountability.
The product complements incumbent registers or GRC systems where useful instead of requiring customers to replace them wholesale.
Pricing, gross margin, retention, analyst-hour savings, partner conversion, and the 140-customer growth path are unvalidated commercial hypotheses.
Security assurance, regulatory QA, and support are delegated as needed before the founder attempts production scale alongside employment.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: DORA creates a live, recurrent, relational register spanning entities, contracts, services, functions, providers, subcontractors, and locations. The low dry-run pass rate supports a real data-quality problem, and cell-level contract provenance is a more useful control point than another spreadsheet formatter.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Every in-scope entity must maintain the register, supervisory use is operational, and published competitor prices show some budget for solving it. The evidence does not show that provenance warrants a separate premium, and most non-passing dry-run registers failed only a small share of checks, so remediation may be episodic.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Onboarding and recurring per-workspace fees are credible, with competitor pricing providing a realistic range. Low-cost annual plans cap simple-register pricing, while procurement, secure hosting, extraction QA, taxonomy maintenance, partner enablement, and support pressure CAC, margins, payback, and part-time owner earnings; none is measured.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Payments, e-money, insurance, and investment groups plus compliance outsourcers form a broad mandated EU market, and a Polish complex-group or partner wedge is bounded enough to start. Small entities have limited vendor inventories and budgets, so economic meaning depends on targeting groups or aggregated portfolios.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Multiple DORA-native tools already provide validation, audit trails, and regulator-ready exports, and Venvera overlaps the proposed upstream contract-analysis wedge. Provenance and graph reconciliation may win difficult cases, but they do not yet support a credible path to segment dominance against specialists, consultants, and GRC suites.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A trusted contract-to-control evidence graph could extend into wider DORA third-party risk, contract remediation, outsourcing oversight, related resilience regimes, and multi-client compliance operations. Expansion depends on security credibility and accurate taxonomies rather than being automatic.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Deep integrations, approved mappings, and recurrent defect patterns could create switching friction and improve over time. Public rules are non-exclusive, confidential contracts restrict cross-client learning, data must remain segregated, and established vendors can add provenance or extraction features.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Cell-level evidence and graph reconciliation could reduce manual tracing and make complex submissions easier to defend. No observed extraction accuracy, review-time reduction, resubmission avoidance, or advantage over Venvera and existing register tools establishes that the improvement is large enough to change buying behavior.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: DORA has applied since 2025, reporting is operational, and the first critical-provider designations confirm ongoing supervisory use. The initial implementation surge may already be passing by 2026, making recurring contract updates and remediation—not one-time setup—the necessary timing thesis.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: DORA advisers, MSPs, specialist law firms, and compliance outsourcers could aggregate customers and reduce direct selling. No partner commitment exists, these parties may already use competing tools, and a new vendor handling confidential contracts faces high trust and procurement hurdles.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder is well matched to document AI, graphs, validation, and quantitative QA, and a customer-controlled remediation pilot can fit the stated capital. Multilingual contract accuracy, hierarchical edge cases, confidential-data security, financial-sector procurement, regulatory review, incident response, and human validation make production demanding for a part-time solo founder.

main_structural_strength: A mandatory, relational register must remain current as contracts and provider chains change, giving a human-approved, cell-level provenance layer a recurring operational control point rather than only a reporting-date use case.
primary_score_limiter: The differentiation is narrow and unvalidated in a price-anchored category where incumbents already offer validation, exports, audit trails, and some contract analysis, while the proposed product's access to confidential contracts creates additional procurement friction.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Several tools already provide regulator-ready register workflows at transparent low prices, Venvera advertises contract-clause checking, and most dry-run failures involved fewer than five of 116 checks, suggesting many buyers may need only modest episodic remediation.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid partner or complex-group pilot should secure approved contract access, demonstrate high field-level accuracy with bounded human-review time, prevent a failed validation or remove 40 to 100 analyst hours, pass the buyer's security review, and convert to recurring use triggered by real contract updates.
highest_value_structural_change: Position the product as a deploy-in-client-tenant provenance and reconciliation engine for compliance outsourcers managing complex groups and subcontractor chains, integrating with incumbent register tools instead of replacing them; this concentrates on hard cases and reduces both CAC and sensitive-data objections.
